To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a solid-electrolyte interphases (SEI) can be formed on lithium metal electrodes by immersing the lithium in ionic liquid (IL) based electrolytes, resulting in long-lived Li|IL|LiFePO _{4} cells.
a simple, industrially applicable pretreatment of lithium metal anodes using ionic liquids allows long-lived batteries.
a simple, industrially applicable, lithium metal pretreatment method can result in a commercially viable battery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel materials for the next generation of lithium-ion batteries.
the development and characterization of ionic liquids for the use as electrolytes in lithium metal batteries.
the development of new materials and technologies for energy storage and conversion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pretreatment of lithium metal anodes in ionic liquid-based electrolytes can be used to create an effective, long-lasting solid electrolyte interphase, resulting in the safe cycling of lithium metal batteries.

the use of ionic liquid electrolyte and a simple pretreatment process of immersion of the lithium metal electrode in the electrolyte before battery construction results in the formation of a stable and protective solid electrolyte interface that enables the long-term cycling of Li|electrode|LiFePO _{4} batteries.

the pretreatment process results a durable and lithium-ion permeable solid-electrolyte inter-phase that allows safe charge-discharge cycling of commercially-applicable Li||LiFePO4 cells for 1, 000 cycles with coulombic efficiency greater than 99.5%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an effective method to prevent lithium dendrite formation and improve the safety of Li-metal batteries.
a simple, industrially applicable lithium anode pre-treatment process is shown to result in a long cycle life in lithium metal batteries.
we have developed a facile process to stabilize lithium metal using 3D-printed ionic liquid electrolyte, which allows the lithium metal anode to achieve long cycle life and high Coulombic efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it shows that the formation of an effective solid electrolyte interphase on the surface of lithium electrodes can be achieved using a variety of ionic liquids, and that this solid–electroliyte interphase is effective for preventing dendritic growth during cycling.
the pretreatment of lithium metal electrodes with ionic liquid electrolyte can be applied to a wide range of lithium metal battery chemistries.

a pretreatment step of the Li metal electrode in a room temperature ionic liquids containing lithium salts is sufficient to form a protective layer on the Li metal electrode, which is able to prevent Li dendrite formation during battery cycling.
